newsitem.title: singapore: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel shrugs off Indian tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel shrugs off Indian tender.

text.p: Singapore middle distillates prices ignored India's import tender with gas oil slipping further on ample prompt supplies, traders said on Tuesday.
At least five gas oil offers emerged late Tuesday with one offer slipping to $22.15 per barrel for July 2-6 loading, jet cargoes were offered at $23.45.
But bids were scarce, traders said.
On Monday, a 150,000 barrel cargo for July 1-5 lifting was traded at $22.20 per barrel free on board (fob) -- lowest in 18-months.
Traders said the prompt market for both gas oil and jet remained awashed with barrels.
They said the widening of the July and August time spread for gas oil indicated that players are shifting their focus to the foward months market where fundamentals are healthier.
July/August spread has widened to minus 55 cents to minus 40 cents.

Traders the arbitrage from Europe to the East is closed currently, keeping a lid on supplies. They said this helps the foward market. They added the current overhang should be cleared by then as China gradually absorbs the excess barrels.
A western trader was heard offering end June to early July cargo at a 20-cent discount to Singapore spot quotes fob compared to last week's flat to 10 cents premium.

India has issued two term tenders to buy a total of 1.44 million barrels of 0.5-percent, 0.25 percent and 1.0 percent sulphur diesel and 360,000 barrels of superior kerosene for delivery between August 1997 and March 1998.
Both tenders close July 2 and is valid until July 6.
Traders said refinery cuts at Shell Singapore would also help to support prices.
Shell Singapore has begun its planned crude runs cut today. In a move to reduce average June runs from 59,000 tonnes per day todate to 57,000 tonnes per day, it reduced runs by 2,000 tonnes per day.
Indonesia July and August purchases are also expected to increase due to shutdown of crude units at Balikpapan and Cilacap refineries for maintenance.
